skill.name: agy-worker
skill.description: Delegates scoped repository exploration and implementation to Google Antigravity CLI, then supports Codex review, verification, repair, and controlled delivery.
skill.summary: Delegate bounded repository work to Antigravity while keeping approval and final acceptance with Codex.
skill.author: cagdasyurekli

security_audit.summary: The review confirmed intentional high-impact capabilities: external provider execution, repository-content transmission, verifier command execution, and limited private configuration access. Most static matches are false positives from defensive validation, documentation, compact schemas, or fixed local commands. Default session mode lacks host containment, and 589 lower-priority static matches remain outside the supplied adjudication set. Static review was capped at 400/989 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 589 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Session isolation is the default despite retaining normal user filesystem and network authority.
remediation.suggestion: Default to native or equivalent containment where supported. Require a separate prominent confirmation when session mode is selected.

remediation.issue: Whole-worktree approval can expose unrelated repository content to the external provider.
remediation.suggestion: Disable whole-worktree dispatch in the marketplace build, or require scoped manifests unless every path receives explicit review.

remediation.issue: Legacy shell verification executes caller-selected text through bash.
remediation.suggestion: Remove shell mode from the default workflow. Prefer validated argv verification and require a separate warning for any retained shell mode.

remediation.issue: Native mode grants the security helper broader Keychain operations than token lookup requires.
remediation.suggestion: Replace helper access with a least-privilege credential handoff that cannot add, modify, delete, or enumerate unrelated Keychain items.

remediation.issue: Static review was capped at 400 of 989 matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual review of the remaining 589 matches before automatic publication or installation is enabled.

semantic_findings.title: Approved repository content is transmitted to an external provider
semantic_findings.description: Scoped files or an entire approved worktree can be readable and transmissible to Google or Gemini. Digest approval reduces accidental scope changes but does not eliminate third-party disclosure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly documents provider-readable content, whole-worktree transmission, and the need to remove secrets before launch.

semantic_findings.title: Default session isolation retains ambient user authority
semantic_findings.description: The default session mode gives AGY normal user filesystem and network authority outside the staged workspace. Scope reconciliation cannot prevent unobserved reads or network activity.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both the primary instructions and security guide state that session mode has no host containment and cannot observe access outside the stage.

semantic_findings.title: Native mode grants broad Keychain helper and listener authority
semantic_findings.description: Native mode can expose wildcard listeners and broader same-user Keychain operations through the security helper. Approval does not technically limit helper operations to one AGY token.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The security guide explicitly states that wildcard binds are possible and Keychain reads, additions, changes, and deletions may be allowed.

high_findings.title: Hidden file in home directory
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The optional account phase reads ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json from the user's home directory. The action is documented and explicit, but it accesses private tool configuration.

high_findings.title: Process exec
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The native sandbox profile explicitly allows the provider process to execute the bound target and tools from staged and system paths. This is required functionality, but it grants meaningful command-execution authority.

content.user_title: Delegate Repository Work with Verified Boundaries
content.value_statement: Complex repository tasks can consume Codex context and still produce weak evidence. This skill delegates bounded work to Antigravity while preserving review and acceptance controls.
actual_capabilities: Previews provider-readable repository content before any live dispatch.
Stages selected files in an owner-private Gitless directory for scoped jobs.
Runs explore, task, and project workflows with bounded cycle budgets.
Binds approvals, state, and candidate artifacts with SHA-256 digests.
Reconciles only authorized staged changes into the source worktree.
Records driver-owned verification and final acceptance evidence.
limitations: Only Codex hosts are supported; Claude and Claude Code hosts are not supported.
Live dispatch requires Antigravity, provider access, Git, Bash, and Python 3.
Session isolation does not restrict AGY from the user's filesystem or network.
Worker output remains untrusted until Codex reviews the diff and runs checks.

use_cases.title: Explore an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Delegate bounded architecture discovery, then have Codex verify important claims against selected files.

use_cases.title: Implement a focused change
use_cases.description: Stage approved files, request a bounded implementation, and reconcile only authorized edits after review.
use_cases.target_user: Maintainers handling scoped features or repairs

use_cases.title: Coordinate a verified project workflow
use_cases.description: Run several controlled cycles, preserve candidate work, and bind independent checks before final acceptance.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a repository area
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agy-worker to explore [directory]. Identify the main components and dependencies. Verify important claims against the repository before reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a bounded task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agy-worker to implement [change]. Allow edits only under [paths]. Review the diff and run [test command] before acceptance.

prompt_templates.title: Dispatch with selected content
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a provider scope for [files]. Preview the exact readable content and write subset. Ask for approval before dispatching with [model].

prompt_templates.title: Run a verified project workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project workflow for [goal] with at most [cycles] cycles. Preserve partial work, request bounded repairs, and finalize only after independent checks.

output_examples.input: Explore the parser package and explain its error flow.
output_examples.output: A scoped exploration report lists the files reviewed, traces the main error paths, and separates verified facts from coverage limits.

output_examples.input: Add timeout tests under the networking test directory.
output: A reviewed candidate changes only approved test files.
The relevant test command and result are recorded as driver-owned evidence.
Final status states whether the candidate is verified, partially verified, rejected, or blocked.

output_examples.input: Repair a failed check without widening repository access.
output_examples.output: A same-scope repair request includes sanitized failure details, preserves the approved model and budget, and produces a new candidate for review.

best_practices: Use a selected-file provider scope for every bounded task.
Remove secrets and unrelated private files before approving provider-readable content.
Review exact candidate bytes and run independent checks before final acceptance.
anti_patterns: Do not treat installation or a preview digest as provider authorization.
Do not use session isolation when ambient filesystem or network access is unacceptable.
Do not trust worker-reported tests as independent verification evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill support Claude or Claude Code hosts?
faq.answer: No. The runtime supports Codex hosts only, although a provider model name may contain Claude.

faq.question: Does installation send repository data to Google?
faq.answer: No. Live dispatch requires a separate approval for the exact provider-readable scope and isolation mode.

faq.question: What is the safest dispatch mode?
faq.answer: Use selected-file scope with native containment where supported. Review the preview and remove sensitive content before approval.

faq.question: Can the worker edit any repository file?
faq.answer: Scoped jobs reconcile only approved write paths. Whole-worktree mode exposes a broader boundary and needs explicit approval.

faq.question: Are worker test results trusted?
faq.answer: No. Codex must inspect the candidate and run driver-owned checks before reporting acceptance.

faq.question: What happens when verification fails?
faq.answer: The workflow preserves useful candidate work and can request a bounded same-conversation repair when prior approval permits it.
